title: "Contribute to MMA"
description: "MMA is an open-source resource. Contributions from the community are encouraged. This page describes how you can create and share resources to improve MMA."

Before contributing, it's a good idea to read the [MMA website
README](webpage_README.qmd). In particular, webpages are created using [Quarto
Markdown](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html). We prefer
that you contributions match the expected syntax as much as possible: these are
the pages that will get published the fastest. If that is too much of a barrier,
you can send anything you would like to share to us. Publishing may take longer,
but we will work on getting it published. 

Every submission is read by the website maintainers before it is published to
the site.

::: {.callout-note}
Contributions to MMA are property of the author (you!) and will be credited as
such. If there is significant work from someone else (e.g., getting it to the
correct format), they may also be credited. 

All contributions to MMA must match the MMA license. 
:::

The steps for contributing to MMA are below. 

## Step 1: Write your page
Please read the [MMA website README](webpage_README.qmd)! Contributions that
closely match the preferred format take priority and are published quicker!

### Option 1 (Preferred):
Download the template that fits what you are contributing, fill it in, and
keep the file ending in `.qmd`.

- [Topic page template (hub)](_templates/hub.qmd){download="hub-template.qmd"}:
  a new application topic (for example, Titration).
- [Connection template](_templates/connection.qmd){download="connection-template.qmd"}:
  one application topic used with one math topic.
- [Resource template](_templates/resource.qmd){download="resource-template.qmd"}:
  a lesson, worksheet or problem set that belongs to an existing connection.

### Option 2 (Not preferred, but totally fine if learning qmd is a barrier!)
Send whatever you have. LaTeX is preferred, but a word document is also okay.
Please try to match the format of existing pages as much as possible.


### Include the following with your submission
Include:
  - your **name and affiliation**, if you would like to be credited on the page.
  - Any **figures or a reference file** (`.bib`) the page uses. If there is
    more than one file, put them all in a single zip file.


## Step 2: Send it to us
MMA needs contributions to thrive. We want to make this efficient, but we also
don't want to add barriers to contributing. There are many ways to contribute to
MMA. Choose whichever submission method below that works for you. The options
below are listed in the order of easiest for you (hardest for us) to hardest for
you (easiest for us). We prefer the Option 4, but don't let that stop you from
contributing!

### Option 1: Email (easiest for contributors)

Attach your file(s) to an email to
[jupsal@uw.edu](mailto:jupsal@uw.edu?subject=MMA%20Page%20Submission) with
the subject line **MMA Page Submission**. In the message, say who you are
and how you would like to be credited.

### Option 2: Google Form

[Submit through the Google form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxOhbR5HnVKtemq2Vtk8LiF4z-SpC-qmdEo1_gMrLqq0bvZA/viewform?usp=publish-editor). The form asks for your
name, affiliation, a short description, and the file. You should include your email as well in case there are any questions. 


### Option 3: GitHub pull request (easiest for maintainers)

If you already use GitHub, or want to learn, this is the best option: your
change is reviewed, tracked, and credited to you automatically. See
[how to contribute with GitHub](webpage_README.qmd#sec-github), or send
Jeremy your GitHub username to be added to the repository.


## What happens next

The maintainers read your submission, may write back with questions or
suggestions, and then adds it to the site. You will be told when it is live.
